title: Console Optimize: transactional recommendation journey with staged apply & audit-safe rollback
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Customers want automated batching/caching recommendations surfaced in Console Optimize, but applying suggested config changes (batch sizes, cache TTLs, prefix caching rules) risks regressions in latency or output quality. We need a workflow that lets PMs/engineers preview diffs, stage or canary applies, and have an immutable audit trail with one-click safe rollback.

Goal: Deliver a Console UX flow that surfaces per-route recommendation cards, a rich diff preview with simulated cost/latency delta, and a transactional apply pipeline that produces a tamper-proof apply record and a fast rollback button. The UX should make safety guarantees explicit (canary percentage, fallback model/variant), and integrate with Console rollouts and runtime metrics.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement the inference runtime automation (actual auto-tuning engine) nor enterprise RBAC policy enforcement beyond simple enable/disable flags. It also does not include long-term retention/archival of audit logs beyond 90 days (handled by infra).
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation cards appear on per-route Optimize pages with concise rationale, estimated token-cost delta, and confidence score.
Clicking a card opens a diff preview modal that displays old vs new config, estimated cost/latency impact (worst/median/best), and links to example prompts used for impact estimation.

Apply flow supports: Dry-run (preview only), Staged/canary apply (percentage & time window), and Immediate apply. Each apply creates an immutable Apply Record with unique ID, timestamp, user, and parameters.
Console shows a timeline for each Apply Record (created, started, canary metrics, promoted, rolled back) and stores links to related GitHub PRs / PR numbers if an infra change is required.

Rollback button reverts runtime config to the previous stable variant and records a Rollback event in the audit trail. Rollback completes within SLO (config propagation <= 2 minutes for hosted routes).
Audit trail entries are exportable (CSV) and include who applied the change, which routes were affected, pre/post snapshots, and an optional free-text rationale.

E2E smoke test: create recommendation, perform staged apply to 10% traffic for 30 minutes, observe canary metrics and promote. Rollback during canary correctly returns traffic and metrics reflect reverted config.
implementation_notes: Frontend: new RecommendationCard component with quick stats, CTA to open DiffPreviewModal. Reuse existing Rollouts primitives where possible.
Backend: Introduce ApplyRecord model (immutable). API endpoints: POST /optimize/apply (dry-run/staged/immediate), GET /optimize/apply/:id, POST /optimize/apply/:id/rollback.
Telemetry: Emit events: recommendation.view, recommendation.apply.started, apply.canary.metrics, apply.promote, apply.rollback. Include sampling for request-level traces.
Runtime contract: staged apply must support traffic-splitting by percentage for hosted and Dedicated routes. If Dedicated cannot split, UI must grey out staged option and show reason.
Safety: apply endpoint requires re-auth for users without "apply_without_2fa" flag; guard against concurrent applies by queuing conflicting ApplyRecords.
Data: Store pre/post config snapshots (stringified) in ApplyRecord to guarantee replayability and auditability; retention 90 days.
Dependencies: requires ENG work to add ApplyRecord DB table and rollout API (ENG-4412), and DES work for diff visual language and spacing (DES-330).
Release: feature gate behind console-2025.03 rollout flag; enable for 10% of orgs initially.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal alpha (console-staging) with DevRel and 2 pilot customers. Phase 2: Beta opt-in via feature flag for 10% orgs. Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% after two weeks of no major regressions. Monitoring: cost delta, p95 latency, error rate, rollback frequency. If rollback rate > 1% or p95 latency increases by > 15% within 24h, pause rollout.
